evidence: StageSnapshot persists stage_id, snapshot_id, node_uid, lineage_id, metric facts and source_event.
Workspace snapshots use SHA-256 content-addressed objects and manifests; restore preflights every referenced object before target mutation.
discover_all keeps snapshots addressable by stable node_uid instead of collapsing same visible stage IDs.
resume rehydrates active stage snapshots from the atomic stage map and falls back to discovered snapshots; lineage is reconstructed from loaded snapshot lineage IDs.
A public test creates two archived S01 snapshots from different lineage node_uids and verifies pending ESTRA restores the explicitly requested old node_uid while keeping both in archive.
archived_anchor_identity.scope_limit: This establishes identity selection when a pending ESTRA transaction already exists in memory and establishes snapshot rehydration after restart; it does not establish persistence of the pending ESTRA decision itself across process death.

evidence: Before restoring an archived Stage, SnapshotStore captures a terminal archive of the live workspace.
On ordinary exceptions during SnapshotStore.restore, it attempts terminal-archive rollback and raises if both restore and rollback fail.
Public tests exercise restore failure and a post-restore failure and verify rollback behavior.
Per-file restore uses atomic copies and CAS object digest verification.
hard_kill_gap: pending_estra is an in-memory solver attribute; no durable pending-ESTRA journal/replay path was found in the public source.
The terminal archive is durable, but no startup reconciler was found that scans an incomplete ESTRA transaction and automatically rolls it back or forward after SIGKILL/process death.
A hard kill between workspace clearing and complete restore can therefore leave a partially restored live workspace even though the terminal archive exists.
The provided lnr_kill_resume.sh escalates a still-running matching process to SIGKILL after one second, so hard-kill recovery is an operationally relevant boundary.

evidence: lhr_stage_map.json is written using an atomic write helper.
stage ledger validation enforces append-only stage ordering and one next-stage append at a time.
lhr_stage_performance.csv is appended with csv.DictWriter rather than a transaction journal.

LHR state events are appended to JSONL and compact lhr_state.json is then atomically replaced; a crash between these operations can leave the compact state behind the event stream until a rebuild/aggregation path runs.
stage_and_evaluation_observability.scope_limit: No public crash-injection test was found that kills the process at each ESTRA phase and asserts equality of stage map, stage ledger, performance ledger and evaluation-consumption state against an uninterrupted reference.

evidence: Parallel-run resume budget accounting persists charged_elapsed_sec, resume_prior_charged_elapsed_sec and resume_total_budget_sec in logs/state.json; remaining-policy resumes spend logical budget minus charged elapsed, while fresh-policy grants the configured segment budget.
External-LLM failure classes can be explicitly uncharged.
UnifiedResourceStore protects resource_state.json with an exclusive file lock and atomic os.replace, and appends resource events under a separate lock.
gap: Parallel runner task state uses direct state_file.write_text in observed running/finalization paths rather than the atomic resource-state helper; malformed JSON is read as an empty state. A parent/controller crash during that write can therefore lose charged-budget/controller metadata.
This write-risk is scoped to the parallel-run task state path; it does not negate the stronger atomic resource_state.json implementation.

covered: single pending tool-call detection and direct execution
continuation after a persisted tool result
resource resume events and resumed-bash heartbeat
exact archived-node restore when pending_estra is already present
ordinary-exception rollback during or after archived-stage restore
not_observed: process kill immediately after ESTRA decision but before restore
process kill after terminal archive creation but before workspace restore completes
process kill after workspace restore but before memory/stage-map/lineage commit completes
restart-equivalence assertion for charged budget plus evaluation-consumption cursor
kill-point matrix asserting exact action chronology equivalence

design_hypothesis.name: proof-carrying recovery transaction
required_durable_fields: source lineage and intended successor lineage
design_hypothesis.recovery_rule: At startup, reconcile any non-done transaction by idempotent roll-forward only when all phase preconditions and content digests match; otherwise restore the pre-transaction terminal archive and controller/evaluation/budget cursors. Never infer completion from workspace contents alone.
design_hypothesis.matched_test: Run an uninterrupted reference and inject SIGKILL at every durable phase boundary and selected interior points. After resume, compare workspace manifest hash, active node_uid, lineage, stage map, ledger rows, evaluator query IDs, charged budget, resource state, pending tool cursor and final outer result. Require semantic equivalence before claiming crash-safe recovery.

conclusion: ScienceFlow currently provides substantially stronger recovery than a context-only restart: immutable-ish content-addressed Stage snapshots, exact archived-node identity, terminal-archive rollback on ordinary exceptions, tool-call resume and durable resource state. The missing piece is a single durable ESTRA recovery transaction binding action intent, workspace restore, lineage/controller state, budget and evaluation-consumption state across hard process death. Therefore its recovery evidence supports selective artifact-preserving restart, but not arbitrary-kill semantic equivalence of the whole self-improvement controller.
frontier: Search for explicit crash-injection/restart-equivalence tests in another persistent self-improving agent that bind controller action, artifact identity, budget and evaluation-consumption state.

Find a matched multi-action controller experiment comparing at least Continue, clean restart, artifact-preserving restart/rewind and strategy redirect under equal proposal/evaluation budget and a selection-unused outer test.

Retain separate unresolved requirements: candidate-local anytime-valid promotion, proposal-crossing durable statistical spending, bounded selection-feedback bandwidth, immutable artifact identity and complete action/proposal chronology.
